title: Charley Johnson precedes him to New York; the Big Apple
summary: Johnson went to Baron's before Wooding; Wooding does not recall New York being called the Big Apple except for a club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, that year Charley went to Baron's, too. And he played --
And he preceded me there by a year, or a half a year.
I see, so it was later in 1920 that you came to New York to play for Baron Wilkins.
Was New York referred to then as the 'Big Apple', or did that come later?
Did musicians call New York, the 'Big Apple', back in those days.
That would have been later than --
I don't remember calling it the 'Big Apple'.

Because I know there was a place there in New York that we used to all frequent, called the "Big Apple", right across there from Smalls. But I don't remember that statement, that we were in the "Big Apple".
Uh hunh. Well, that Big Apple was still there, on the same corner, 135th and Seventh. Right.

But I don't remember that statement, but I know they came there. Many of them came. But, when we got the word in Atlantic City, Charley had this Matty (Hight) and Mary Stafford, and this other girl I'm talking about. She was a very good singer. She worked with Eubie Blake for awhile. Was also -- was Mabel Richardson. She was from Washington, or down that way. Baltimore and Washington had some terrific girl singers. And a lot of the banjo and guitar players come from there. Washington had good tap dancers. That's where (unintelligible). Philadelphia had piano players.
